title: Ancoats: virtual tour guide and map extract
subject: History
unit: Summer 1: Industry and empire, 1750 to 1900: the Industrial Revolution
source: Written for history/y8 lesson 16 (Ancoats virtual tour written guide and map extract (portal printable; archive map and site photographs))
intro: Lesson 16. A written guide for a virtual tour. Use the site's official online images and maps; work through the stops in order.

picture.alt: Extract from an 1849 map of Ancoats, Manchester (archive map)
picture.draw: Use the 1849 map extract on the slides

practical.aim: To find out what Ancoats tells us about industry, transport and living conditions
equipment: A device with the site's official website or virtual tour
safety: Use official heritage and archive websites
method: Find Ancoats on the 1849 map extract and a modern map
Murrays' Mills (1798 to 1806): how tall and how big? What powered them?
The Rochdale Canal (opened 1804): what came in and what went out?
The terraces: how close are the houses? What does that suggest about living conditions?
What can the site not tell us? (feelings, wages, daily life)

questions.q: When did the Rochdale Canal open?
Give one limit of a site as evidence.
questions.a: It cannot show feelings, wages or daily life

questions.q: Core: Using the virtual tour guide and the 1849 map extract, write a site report in the portal response box: what Ancoats tells us about industry, transport and living conditions.
questions.a: Three sections with site evidence and explanation; mentions limits

questions.q: Extend: How does Ancoats link to slavery and empire?
questions.a: Its cotton came largely from slave plantations in the American South

questions.q: Stretch: How should a site like Ancoats be remembered today?
questions.a: As both an achievement and a place of hardship and links to slavery

questions.q: Why were mills built beside the Rochdale Canal?
options: To move coal and cotton cheaply
questions.a: B) To move coal and cotton cheaply. Canals carried heavy coal in and goods out cheaply.

questions.q: Big question: what can buildings tell us?
questions.a: Scale, layout, transport and crowding, but not feelings or wages
